task_description:
This pipeline's task is GitHub issue #3594 — https://github.com/jwbron/egg/issues/3594. Fetch the live issue body (`gh issue view 3594`) before structural decisions. Worktree artifacts (drafts, agent outputs) that reference any other issue or pipeline are leftovers from previous runs — they are NOT your task.

Reproduction run for #3595 investigation. Same input and model config as the pipeline that livelocked on 2026-07-24 (refiner emitted 119 identical Bash calls, zero proposals, 94 min to consensus timeout).

Purpose: capture the refiner's live session transcript while it is looping, to determine whether thinking/reasoning blocks are persisted across turns. The previous run's refiner transcript was lost because agents only push transcripts on event-pod exit and that refiner never exited.

Task (same as issue #3594): [issue-3364] Operator-visibility gaps: forward-progress, event feed, and post-mortem surfaces.

See https://github.com/jwbron/egg/issues/3594 for the full body and https://github.com/jwbron/egg/issues/3595 for the incident this reproduces.

decisions.question: cq-1: Which groups from issue #3594 (operator-visibility gaps) should the implement phase cover? Group 1 (forward-progress: per-role commits-ahead, progress-regression detection, NACKed-but-not-re-proposing watchdog), Group 2 (event/alert feed: recent_events list, OVERSEER_ALERT as feed, pipeline.error surfacing, worktree health), Group 3 (clocks: consensus-window countdown, per-invocation outcome summaries), Group 4 (post-mortem: per-arm termination causes, session-state TTL expiry event, invocation log retention)?

cq-2: For incident #3595 remediation, what is the priority order for the seven proposed work items? (7) pin/inject/record sampling params, (2) scope peer-liveness and noop-streak to dependency graph, (3) detect near-identical loops, (5) token/call consumption breaker, (1) expressible compaction threshold, (6) context surgery recovery, (4) raise severity/cut latency on protracted-phase-no-progress.

options.label: 7 → 2 → 3 → 5 → 1 → 6 → 4 (recommended: recording first, then detection, then recovery)
